extracted.intended_audience: employers, immigration attorneys, labor economists, small businesses, policy stakeholders, and other commenters on H-1B/H-1B1/E-3 and PERM prevailing wage rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and solicitation of public comment on revised methodologies for computing prevailing wages under H-1B, H-1B1, E-3, and PERM programs, including proposed percentile levels, data sources, and alternatives such as experience-benchmarking and treatment of private surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience Benchmarking methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the sponsored alien worker's wage to the wages earned by U.S. workers with comparable education and experience in the same occupation and geographic area to produce prevailing wages that more closely reflect wages paid to similarly qualified workers in the U.S. labor market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the ACS does not directly measure actual labor market experience, the methodology would estimate 'potential experience' using a commonly accepted definition as age minus years of schooling minus age when schooling begins (often six). Using the OEWS 50th (median), 62nd, 75th, and 90th percentiles for each occupation and geographic area as the base wages, the Department would use public-use microdata from the ACS to generate Mincer wage equations for each occupation among native-born American workers only, modelling the relationship between (log) earnings, educational attainment, and potential experience (measured by age) within each occupation, controlling for area of employment fixed effects. The output would be a matrix of ratios (or wage premia) comparing expected earnings of U.S. workers with each combination of education and potential experience to the overall occupational median, as measured in the ACS. The Department would then apply these ACS-derived ratios to each of the OEWS percentiles to produce Experience Benchmarked wage levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of wage levels under Experience Benchmarking (Levels I–IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each combination of education and experience in each occupation and geographic area would generate a set of four wage levels (Level I–IV) based on percentiles among workers with the same occupation, area, education, and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level I: Typical (50th percentile among workers with same occupation, area, education, and experience) — reflects the median level of skills and typical duties and would be the prevailing wage due an alien worker with a given credential profile. Level II: Specialized (62nd percentile) — reflects a position requiring specialized knowledge, duties, or characteristics that command a premium above the typical wage. Level III: Demanding (75th percentile) — reflects a position requiring a notably higher degree of proficiency, specialized expertise, or responsibility. Level IV: Highly Demanding (90th percentile) — reflects the highest-skilled positions among similarly qualified workers, upper tier of complexity/responsibility/autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of ACS-derived wage premia to OEWS percentiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute prevailing wages by multiplying OEWS percentile wage levels by ACS-derived ratios (wage premia) for each education-experience combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if ACS/Mincer estimates that U.S. accountants with 10 years' experience and a master's earn 20% more than the median, the ratio is 1.2; Level I prevailing wage = OEWS 50th percentile × 1.2; Level II = OEWS 62nd × 1.2; Level III = OEWS 75th × 1.2; Level IV = OEWS 90th × 1.2. This calculation is repeated for every education-experience combination in every occupation and geographic area covered by OEWS (and separately for ACWIA industries as required by statute).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'potential experience' proxy (ACS limitation and estimate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because ACS does not directly measure actual labor market experience, the methodology would estimate 'potential experience' as age minus years of schooling minus typical starting age of schooling (often six).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department invites comment on the effectiveness of using age as a proxy for experience and on sample size, occupational and geographic coverage of ACS, and statistical validity of the modeling approach (e.g., using Mincer wage equations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed percentile levels in this NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM adopts specific wage-percentile targets for the revised four-tier wage structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approach adopted in this NPRM sets wage levels at the 34th, 52nd, 70th, and 88th percentiles — the Department determined these percentiles strike the most appropriate balance between strengthening wage protections and minimizing disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory four-tier requirement (8 U.S.C. 1182(p)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any government survey used to determine prevailing wages must provide at least four levels of wages commensurate with experience, education, and level of supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department has determined that the current implementation of the four-tier structure does not sufficiently differentiate among workers based on these statutory factors and proposes revisions to meet the mandate to prevent adverse effects on U.S. workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevailing wage selection rule for LCA
rubrics_metrics.description: The prevailing wage associated with the LCA is the higher of two items when Experience Benchmarking is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the higher of: (1) the Level I OEWS Level corresponding to the minimum education and experience requirements of the position, and (2) if the alien worker is an H-1B, H-1B1, or E-3 worker, the prevailing wage identified on the Labor Condition Application certified by DOL and listed on the DHS/USCIS I-129 Petition for Nonimmigrant Worker approved for that alien worker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer LCA filing procedures under Experience Benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers must account for education-experience profiles when filing LCAs and when no alien worker is identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OFLC search would be updated to reflect prevailing wage levels of different education and experience profiles; if the employer has not identified an alien worker, it would file the LCA for each education-experience profile it would consider for the role, and the eventual hire would be paid under the relevant LCA matching that alien worker's education-experience profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and information collection burden (forms and PRA considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether revised prevailing wage methodology requires changes to information collections and the burden such changes would impose on employers and applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the alternative bases prevailing wage determinations on the alien worker's actual education and experience rather than the employer's description of minimum job requirements, the Department invites comment on administrative feasibility and burden of providing this information on revised Forms ETA-9035 and ETA-9141 and similar Appendix A information on ETA-9089. The Department has determined that the proposed changes do not require a PRA collection subject to OMB approval and would not affect existing OMB-controlled collections (OMB Control Nos. 1205-0508, 1205-0310, 1205-0451).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation for public comment topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific areas on which the Department solicits feedback from stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department invites public comment on all aspects of Experience Benchmarking and alternatives, including: strengths and limitations of using the ACS (sample size, occupational/geographic coverage); effectiveness of using age as proxy for experience; efficacy of employing Mincer wage equations; appropriateness of establishing base OEWS wage levels at the chosen percentiles; statistical validity of applying ACS-derived ratios to OEWS; whether other data sources (including administrative records) could provide more precise estimates; and overall administrative feasibility and burden on employers/applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and permissible use of private wage surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of private wage surveys in prevailing wage determinations and standards for acceptance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considered eliminating private surveys but rejected that alternative to preserve employer flexibility in specialized markets. The Department will retain private surveys in limited circumstances, monitor their use to prevent abuse, and reserve the right to reject any private survey that does not meet methodological standards or otherwise fails to satisfy regulatory requirements. The Department invites comment on whether further limitations or safeguards on private surveys would be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: National wage standard alternative constraint (area-of-intended-employment requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of replacing area-specific prevailing wages with a national wage standard for remote/distributed work and the statutory/legal constraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although a national standard could simplify compliance and reflect nationalized labor markets, the Department declined it due to statutory language in the INA requiring prevailing wages to be based on the 'area of intended employment,' potential disproportionate impacts on employers in lower-wage regions, and need for further stakeholder engagement and legal analysis. The Department may revisit the alternative in future rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) impact analysis criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and methodology for assessing significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA (and SBREFA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department must prepare an IRFA/FRFA when proposing/issuing regulations with significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities. For this NPRM the Department estimated one-time familiarization cost ($60.94) and average annual wage cost per small entity ($20,298), used a 3% of revenue threshold as 'significant individual impact,' and assumed 15% of impacted small entities would exceed that threshold to determine whether a substantial number are affected. These thresholds are consistent with prior rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) compliance rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may not conduct or sponsor a collection of information unless approved by OMB and displaying a valid OMB control number; the public is not required to respond without a valid OMB number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department determined the proposed changes to computation of prevailing wage levels, based on existing OEWS data, do not require a new PRA collection or affect existing collections covered by OMB Control Numbers cited; thus no additional OMB approval is being sought for those covered collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Orders and administrative-review standards to be met
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory review obligations under multiple Executive Orders (13132 federalism, 13175 tribal consultation, 12988 civil justice reform) and the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department must examine constitutional/statutory authority and effects on States (E.O. 13132), assess tribal implications (E.O. 13175), and ensure regulations eliminate drafting errors/ambiguity, minimize litigation, provide clear legal standards, define retroactivity, and adequately define key terms (E.O. 12988). Under UMRA, assess whether the rule imposes unfunded mandates exceeding the statutory threshold (e.g., $100 million) and prepare a written statement if so. The Department asserts it has reviewed and met or reasonably addressed these standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objectives and legal basis for the NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM's stated objectives and statutory basis guiding the proposed revisions to prevailing wage methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives: strengthen wage protections for U.S. workers, align prevailing wage levels with actual market wages, reduce incentive to prefer alien workers due to wage differentials, ensure compliance with INA sections (8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(5)(A), 1182(n)(1)(A), 1182(t)(1)(A), and 1182(p)(4)), and promote integrity/effectiveness of foreign labor certification programs. The NPRM is responsive to Presidential directive and grounded in the Department's authority to administer labor certification and interpret the INA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of benefits and burdens (policy trade-offs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulated primary benefits of the Experience Benchmarking approach and anticipated burdens on employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary benefits claimed: ends practice of wage arbitrage, improves ability to screen for exceptional talent, reduces employer ability to under-classify workers. Anticipated burdens: employers must collect actual education/experience information on applications, learn a new system, and may no longer be able to engage in wage arbitrage; small entities may face increased wage costs and compliance time. The Department invites comment on these trade-offs and whether alternatives (e.g., delayed implementation for small entities) are appropriate.
